_about: Published prices for the add-ons a traveller can put on the bill: wifi, seat choice, an extra-legroom seat, priority boarding, a lounge day pass, and travel insurance as a share of the ticket. Researched from the airlines' own pages and re-checked by a second reader (2026-09-25, per Patrick). build.py inlines only the prices; the sources stay here.
_method: Keyed by the airline flying the longest flight. Each row has a 'long' and a 'short' price in US cents (short-haul: a trip inside one border, or no flight over four hours). 'from': true marks a published starting price (the airline's cheapest), which the page still marks with its estimate asterisk. 'free': a sentence when the airline gives it away (to everyone, or to members of its free loyalty programme). Foreign-currency prices are converted at the rate on the as_of date and say so. A figure with no primary source is left out, and the page falls back to its typical price, marked.

insurance.note: A comprehensive trip policy as a share of the trip cost. The insurers' trade association says 4% to 8%; Squaremouth, a marketplace reporting its own sales, says 4% to 10%, about 6% in 2026 and 6.5% over 25 Aug to 24 Sep 2026. Neither sets premiums, so it stays an estimate, marked. The page applies it to the ticket.
